statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail risk 3% (low), with no Nasdaq-100 price path observable inside the CME weekend halt, against Stress of 66% (high) while the Strait of Hormuz stays closed, four vessel strikes have been reported since 1 October, and Tehran reviews Washington's response to its seven-day reopening proposal.
recommendation: Tail remains far below the block threshold, so the mapped policy state stays EA_ON. A narrow danger window is published across the 22:00Z CME reopen and the hour after it, 00:00-02:00 Berlin on 5 October, where the published forecast Tail path reaches the WATCH band on gap and thin-liquidity discontinuity risk rather than on observed structure.
headline: Hormuz stays shut and Tehran weighs Washington's reply while Tail holds at its halt-session floor, with CME futures closed until 22:00Z
body: CME equity-index futures have been halted since Friday 21:00Z and reopen at 22:00Z on 4 October, so no Nasdaq-100 price path exists to assess and Tail stays at its structural floor of 3%. The last observed structure was orderly and two-way: the cash index set a record intraday high of 31,017.53 on Friday 2 October, gave it back in full, and closed at a record 30,807.93, up 1.00% from a 30,501.60 previous close, in the lower half of its 30,737.07-31,017.53 range. A record close that surrenders its own high is mean-reversion-friendly rather than evidence of a persistent one-way path, which is why Tail is held at the floor even as the geopolitical backdrop stays unresolved. Stress is high at 66%. The Strait of Hormuz, which carries roughly a fifth of global oil and LNG trade, remains closed to commercial transits, with one transit recorded on 27 September against a pre-crisis baseline near 85 a day and about 188 AIS-visible vessels holding position away from port. Four vessel strikes have been reported in the strait since 1 October, the most recent on Sunday with engine-room damage. Parliament speaker Qalibaf restated on Sunday that the waterway stays shut until Iran's seven Islamabad Memorandum conditions are met, while deputy foreign minister Gharibabadi said Tehran is reviewing Washington's response to the seven-day proposal Araghchi outlined in New York. Both tracks are therefore live and unresolved, which is a Stress and Confidence matter rather than a Tail one under the published contract. Against that, the pricing of risk is notably calm: VIX closed at 15.31, down 6.59%, WTI fell about 1.9% to roughly $91 as the G7 prepared to release 100 million barrels of reserves, and a third US carrier strike group is reported en route to the region. The macro backdrop is softer but not easier. September payrolls came in at +29,000 against +90,000 expected, unemployment rose to 4.2%, wage growth slowed to 3.0% year on year and prior months were revised down by 60,000, yet Treasury yields reversed higher into Friday's close, with the 2-year near 4.84% and the 10-year near 5.29%, and October hike odds settled around 15-16%. An elevated long end alongside a weakening labour market is a persistent stressor, not an observed path risk. Confidence is high at 87%: Friday's closing levels, yields, oil, VIX, the Sunday geopolitical record and the week's calendar are all verified, while the one genuine gap is the absence of any live price path during the weekend halt. The shared Finviz context file was not usable this run, with a collection timestamp of 29 September and a partial collection status, so this assessment rests entirely on independent research. The danger window is deliberately narrow and covers the 22:00Z reopen and the hour after it, where the published forecast Tail path reaches the WATCH band on gap and discontinuity risk; it decays from 00:00Z on the base case that reopening discovery is orderly and two-way, and would have to be revised upward instead if price were observed holding a session extreme with shallow pullbacks.

lookbackSummary: Across the past 24 published hours Claude held Tail at 3% in every slot, with every hour mapping to EA_ON and green and the dominant mode normal throughout. Stress rose from 58% at 17:00Z on 3 October to a 79% ceiling at 09:00Z on 4 October as the weekend geopolitical checkpoints opened, then eased through 73%, 70%, 68% and 64% as those checkpoints resolved into stated positions, before firming to 66% and 67% late in the window once the Sunday strike and the restated reopening conditions were verified. Confidence stayed in the 83-88% band.
outlookSummary: The remaining closed Sunday hours carry no scoreable Nasdaq-100 structure, so Tail is held between 3% and 5% through 20:00Z while Stress stays near 66% on the closed strait and the unresolved US-Iran exchange. Tail then steps to 9% in the final closed hour and is raised to 22% and 20%, inside the WATCH band, across the 22:00Z CME reopen and the hour after it, which the published danger window covers. From 00:00Z it decays to 14%, 11% and single digits through the Asian and European sessions on the base case that reopening discovery is orderly and two-way, with Stress easing from 66% to a 58% low. It lifts again to 15% and 16% around Monday's 13:30Z cash open and the 14:00Z ISM Services PMI, both treated as checkpoints rather than automatic blocks, and eases to 14% and 12% afterwards on the assumption the print is absorbed with a normal retracement.
